target.title: fix(release): block stale Codex runtime pins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The stable `@openclaw/codex` package could be published with an older embedded `@openai/codex` runtime even after a newer stable Codex release was available. Operators then saw the plugin as current because the updater correctly compared the published OpenClaw plugin version, while the route still launched the older runtime bundled by that package.

The canonical failure is release-time dependency freshness, not host CLI discovery or runtime binary attribution. On June 30, 2026, `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` was published with `@openai/codex@0.139.0` even though `@openai/codex@0.142.4` had already been published on June 29, 2026. The release pipeline validated internal package consistency but had no independent source of truth for whether the selected executable dependency was current.

Closes #99951.
Supersedes #99956 with the release-owner fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps the invariant at the owner boundary:

- `@openclaw/codex` opts `@openai/codex` into a strict release-freshness contract through plugin metadata.
- The generic plugin release checker validates that each configured package is an exact runtime dependency.
- Release checks and release-plan collection resolve npm's `latest` dist-tag independently and fail closed when the pinned version is stale or cannot be verified.
- The check is opt-in, so ordinary plugin dependencies are not forced onto latest.

The Codex runtime is updated from `0.142.4` to `0.142.5`, generated lock data is refreshed, and the harness model snapshot is regenerated from the actual `0.142.5` app-server.

This deliberately does not add generic-core Codex version policy, inspect arbitrary selected binaries at runtime, or alter plugin update channel behavior. Those paths cannot prevent the stale artifact from being published and can report false positives for supported alternate routes.

## User Impact

Future Codex plugin releases cannot silently publish an older stable `@openai/codex` executable than npm's current `latest` release. A stale pin or unavailable freshness check blocks the release before users receive another false-green plugin update state.

The dependency bump also moves the next published Codex plugin runtime to `0.142.5`.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: Prevent stale Codex executable pins from passing OpenClaw plugin release validation.

Real environment tested: macOS source checkout with the installed `@openai/codex@0.142.5` app-server, plus an AWS Linux Crabbox `c7a.8xlarge` changed-lane run.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/plugin-npm-release.test.ts test/plugin-clawhub-release.test.ts test/scripts/release-wrapper-scripts.test.ts extensions/codex/src/manifest.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/models.test.ts`
- `node scripts/generate-npm-shrinkwrap.mjs --package-dir extensions/codex --check`
- `node --import tsx scripts/plugin-npm-release-check.ts --plugins @openclaw/codex`
- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --label codex-release-dependency-freshness --timing-json -- env OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed`
- `$autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output`

Evidence after fix:

- 5 focused test files passed across 3 Vitest shards, 76 tests total.
- The Codex shrinkwrap check and live npm-backed plugin release check passed.
- Crabbox run `run_871522b80992` passed the changed gate, including dependency/shrinkwrap guards, full typecheck, lint, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh Codex autoreview returned no actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.83`).
- A real `codex app-server` `model/list` probe reported server version `0.142.5`; the documented public model snapshot was updated from that response.

Observed result after fix: A configured executable dependency below npm `latest`, or a registry failure that prevents verification, rejects plugin release planning instead of accepting a self-consistent stale artifact.

What was not tested: Publishing to npm was not performed. Existing installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` packages remain unchanged until a new plugin release is published and installed.
